evidence.notes: Source states the extra e or ç is kept for je/tu/il/elle/ils/elles but dropped for nous/vous; forms contrast the two paradigms for manger and commencer. Standard conjugation, low uncertainty.

proposals.entity_key: Imparfait vs passé composé with state verbs

evidence.notes: Source says state verbs (être, avoir, penser, croire, savoir, espérer, sembler, paraître) shift meaning in the passé composé; forms show the state (imparfait) vs the specific realization (passé composé). Meaning shift is context-dependent, so exact glosses left out.
Source restricts vouloir to the vous imperative form veuillez used as a polite command; the pair gives the stem change and the veuillez + infinitive pattern. No tu/nous imperative forms exist.

proposals.entity_key: Impersonal expressions followed by the indicative
value: il est vrai que tu as raison
il me semble qu'il est là

evidence.notes: Source lists il est certain, il est sûr, il est évident, il est vrai, il est probable, il me semble as taking the indicative; examples keep the dependent verb in the indicative. Low uncertainty.

proposals.entity_key: Impersonal expressions followed by the subjunctive
value: il vaut mieux que nous partions

evidence.notes: Source lists il faut, il est possible, il vaut mieux among expressions taking the subjunctive; examples show the dependent verb in the subjunctive présent (viennes, pleuve, partions). Low uncertainty.
Source states falloir and pleuvoir occur only in the third-person singular (il faut, il pleut); the transformations record that restriction. No other persons are proposed because they do not exist.

Source gives pleuvoir, neiger, grêler, bruiner used in the impersonal il form without faire; the three listed forms are the concrete impersonal outputs. Grêler omitted only to respect the 3-item limit.
Source gives un/une/des as the indefinite articles and notes the negative form; the pairs show singular to plural and the des -> de/d' change in negation. Low uncertainty.

proposals.entity_key: Indefinite demonstrative pronouns ceci, cela, ça

evidence.notes: Source states cela reflects something already mentioned and ça is the familiar substitute for both; the pairs show the alternations. Register-dependent, so use varies by context.
Source says the preposition à precedes the infinitive after expressions of position (assis, debout, à genoux, accroupi, accoudé); the examples instantiate position + à + infinitive. Low uncertainty.
